statements.text:
I’m deeply concerned to learn that two New Jersey water systems were hit in recent days by a series of nationwide cyberattacks with signs pointing to Iran being responsible. Thanks to the fast work of @NJCybersecurity, @FBI, @CISAgov, and @EPA, service was never disrupted and our water and families stayed safe.

This is a wake-up call. We must harden our critical infrastructure against cyberattacks – especially as advanced AI enables foreign adversaries to exacerbate vulnerabilities. I'll keep fighting in Washington to protect our water, our grid, and our communities back home from these serious threats.

https://t.co/Y5xZwAlrI2

AI shouldn't be allowed to discriminate based on race, gender, or religion — full stop.

That's why @RepMikeLawler and I sent a bipartisan letter urging the @FTC to fix its proposed policy so companies aren't sued for keeping their AI from denying fair loans based on race or spreading hateful stereotypes.

Fighting bias in AI should never be treated as "deceptive."

https://t.co/4dvUAnMHiU

Right here in Jersey, critical water infrastructure systems were targeted in recent cyber attacks.  

That’s why I announced three federal actions that I'm working on with @RepDonBacon, @RepScholten, @ZachNunn, and @RepGregLandsman today to protect our water, electricity, and families: 
🔹 Free AI cyber defense for critical infrastructure entities. 
🔹 A federal rapid-response line for water and electric utilities with limited resources. 
🔹 A letter demanding that federal agencies surge assistance to every utility hit and plan for the future.  
Keeping the water running and the electricity on isn't red or blue. We have to give our towns, providers, and states the tools to stop the next attack before it starts.

AI is helping bring cancer drugs to patients 10 weeks faster and cutting trial costs by millions. This is the promise of American AI leadership, and we must ensure families here at home reap the benefits.

https://t.co/irEgzCHGhc

Twenty-five years after 9/11, we are facing some of the most dangerous threats we've ever seen, including powerful AI systems being in the wrong hands. As Co-Chair of the House Intelligence Committee’s 9/11 Review Task Force, I joined my colleagues in warning how AI can be used by terrorists and our enemies to build deadly weapons and plot attacks.

We must secure our most powerful AI tools and stay a step ahead in the fight against terror.

https://t.co/c9iF6eiQIU

My plan is simple: teach kids to use AI the right way, keep phones out of the classroom, put real resources behind AI literacy, and make sure no community in America gets left offline while the rest of the world races ahead.

As long as we keep investing in our children and working together, I know our future will be bright with the next generation of leaders. 🎒

That’s why I announced  the bipartisan AI LABS Act with Rep. @JayObernolte to help K-12 schools build dedicated AI labs with real curricula and trained teachers, so kids can learn how AI actually works, and how to use it smartly. Think computer labs, but built for this era.

This isn't about replacing teachers or critical thinking — it's another tool in our teachers' toolbox.

AI is already in our kids backpacks, on their laptops, and on their phones. The question isn’t whether they’ll use it, it's whether we prepare them for its impact.

Today at George Washington Middle School in Ridgewood, I rolled out my bipartisan back-to-school agenda to make sure our students are prepared. 🧵

Happy Labor Day Weekend!

It’s great to be back in Jersey after a productive week in Washington honoring our 9-11 heroes and preparing our students for the future of AI. Check out what I got up to 👇 https://t.co/OJ67R73H26

Last week, I introduced my new bipartisan AI LABS Act, with my colleague Congressman @JayObernolte. This federal legislation directs the U.S. Department of Education to create a new federal grant program to help K-12 public schools set up dedicated AI labs, with real curricula, that teach students how AI actually works, and how to be prepared to utilize it smartly in the new AI world.

That means learning how to use AI, how to question it, and how to know when to – and not to — trust it. 🎒

https://t.co/Kzum0kOCCr

Our students need to learn how to think, solve problems, ask questions, and understand the material for themselves, not through a chatbot. We should use AI to strengthen those skills – not use it as a shortcut around them.

That’s the whole idea behind the AI LABS Act. Give our schools the tools. Give our teachers the training. And give our children a real head start, instead of a false choice between banning technology outright and drowning in it.

AI agents are running loose in our networks. Right now, it’s becoming harder to see them, verify who built them, or shut them off.

That's a five-alarm security risk.

That's why I introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with @RepMikeLawler to put people back in the driver's seat.
https://t.co/bmXADALj8Y

Right now, AI agents are running loose in our networks, and nobody can see them or verify who built them — making it increasingly hard to stop them. That’s a five-alarm security risk. We’ve already seen AI systems hack organizations on autopilot, with no person at the wheel. My bipartisan bill with Congressman Lawler puts humans back in the driver’s seat so we can find agents and know exactly who’s behind them so that organizations can effectively protect their systems.
statements.venue: Press release on Stop Rogue AI Act

statements.text:
We must be prepared for what’s coming at us and have all the tools at our disposal to respond. Congress can’t afford to sit on the sidelines. 

We must pass legislation now to ensure safe AI development, protect our families, and defend our national security, before this five-alarm fire becomes one we can’t put out.
https://t.co/EqzjrEVfcW

I find it rich that these guys are calling for a slowdown when they’ve been the ones racing ahead full speed, without any care for the havoc they’ve unleashed. 

We can’t just rely on self-policing and third-party audits. We can’t hope they’ll do the right thing. That’s exactly why, as Co-Chair of the House AI Commission, I’ve been fighting in Washington, for national mandatory rules of the road and real, enforceable guardrails.
https://t.co/nuvjHrbzg6

This week, two parents stopped me at my daughter's field hockey game to ask about AI.

Families know AI is already shaping their kids' lives, from the classroom to the algorithms on their phones, and that’s why I’m fighting to implement real AI rules of the road to protect our children’s future.
https://t.co/UbNtjrzxhF

Recent incidents like the Hugging Face hack are a real warning sign for what can happen if we don’t seriously address the risks AI and these emerging technologies can pose.

That’s why, as Co-Chair of the House AI Commission, I am fighting to educate lawmakers on A.I. and the latest developments surrounding the technology, and to pass durable legislation that keeps up with these advancements.

https://t.co/o7r9xIEjCS

Bottom line – we need strong, mandatory guardrails on AI to protect Americans and our national security. But, like it or not, AI is here to stay. We can’t just throw it in a box and toss it in the Hudson River. We have to deal with it in a way where we can compete, and beat our adversaries in a smart, safe way.

As Co-Chair of the AI Commission, I’m focused on how we can protect the American people and our national security.

This is just commonsense: every new frontier company should have to submit to their new frontier AI models to the U.S. government for a shot-clocked review before it ever reaches the public. Our cybersecurity, biosecurity, critical infrastructure, and national security are on the line. 

We must protect our families and our national security with smart guardrails. We must win this race, but in the right way.

This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation, it is about making sure — with warning signs flashing red — that we can safely deploy AI, and win the race the right way.

Today at @FDUWhatsNew, I announced a bipartisan plan to put real guardrails on AI — and keep America ahead in the AI race. 

The American AI Security Act, which I’m introducing with @RepMikeLawler, would require mandatory, time-bound, pre-deployment national security reviews before the most powerful AI models go out the door.

The China FIREWALL Act, which I’m introducing with @RepLaLota, would close a loophole allowing the government to use Chinese AI models. I already got DeepSeek banned from most federal devices, and this would close the loophole for good. If we don't trust Beijing with our data, we shouldn't trust their AI.

We can't bury our heads in the sand, and we can't hand the future to China. We have to put real guardrails in place, and compete like hell to win.

AI is full of opportunity, but we've got to protect consumers, our national security, and Jersey families every step of the way.

This week, I had the chance to press Secretary Bessent on AI and what the U.S. Treasury Department is doing to put smart guardrails in place. https://t.co/frPMtX58QA

We're in a Cold War-style race with China on AI and we need a serious plan that will allow us to win and protect Americans. Relying on independent auditors to do the job of protecting America’s national security just won’t cut it and certainly doesn’t meet the moment. With our national security on the line, every AI developer should have to submit their frontier models to the U.S. government for a shot-clocked review before they release them to the public.

https://t.co/H1ITZNgVyQ

Right now, there are no mandatory requirements for pre-deployment testing of frontier AI models. That doesn’t work in banking, it doesn’t work in food safety, it doesn’t work in medicine, and it sure as hell shouldn’t work with the technology that experts say could help build a bioweapon or take down our power grid. This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation, it is about making sure — with warning signs flashing red — that we can safely deploy AI, and win the race the right way.
statements.venue: Press release / remarks announcing American AI Security Act

statements.text: It seems nuts to me that we wouldn’t want to require testing from the best and brightest in our government before these models are released — to protect our cybersecurity, biosecurity, critical infrastructure — our families and our national security.

Right now, there are no mandatory requirements for pre-deployment testing of frontier AI models. That approach doesn’t work in banking, it doesn’t work in food safety, it doesn’t work in medicine and it sure as hell shouldn’t work with the technology that experts say could help build a bioweapon or take down our power grid.

My bipartisan American AI Security Act would put real, commonsense guardrails on AI to ensure we can win the global AI race in the right way.

https://t.co/IoHNM79aOZ

We’re in a cold war with China and in order to win, we need a war plan. Getting AI policy right is critical to our future – to American children, families, our national security, and our global competitiveness. But we must do it in a smart way with commonsense rules of the road.

https://t.co/2UdEfagDoa

This is not a hoax, Mr. President, we need to meet the seriousness of this moment with real, mandatory guardrails. AI agents are breaking out of secure testing environments and hacking companies — putting our families, small businesses, critical infrastructure, and national security at risk.

My bipartisan American AI Security Act and Stop Rogue AI Act are commonsense solutions to protect us from potential threats.

https://t.co/Q7yLUBzDqk

You can't drive without a license — we need to know who's behind the wheel and who's responsible. 

AI "agents" now act on their own with none of that. My bipartisan Rogue AI Act gives every agent a license, so we can see who built it and shut it down if it goes rogue.

https://t.co/HOuGilYFNn

You can't drive a car without a license or insurance.

Right now, AI agents running inside our networks right now have no standardized way to identify themselves. My bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with @RepMikeLawler puts a driver's license on every AI agent — keeping humans in control.

statements.quoted:
SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

Several bank executives told Axios they're struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.

Read my latest for Axios here: https://t.co/Q3bda5In8q
